papers.title_en: Beyond the Transcriptome: Chromatin-Informed Prediction of Cell-State-Dependent Perturbation Responses
papers.authors: Jiafa Ruan, Chenyang He, Ruijie Quan, Fanglei Xue, Zongxin Yang, Yi Yang
papers.evidence: 染色质信息驱动的细胞状态相关扰动响应预测
papers.tldr: 现有扰动响应预测多依赖转录组，忽略染色质可及性所反映的细胞状态背景，且难以校正独立采样的对照与扰动群体基线差异。ChromaPert将分子与DNA位点先验同配对对照RNA-ATAC特征结合，并用染色质引导响应路由器CGRR检索对照来源偏移，再以条件传输流学习剩余响应。在K562 CAT-ATAC和Perturb-Multiome的未见靶标与留出状态设定中，其全基因响应相关性最优；迁移已知扰动到留出状态时，全基因相关性提升23.2%，前二十响应基因提升46.2%。该方法表明染色质信息能提升细胞状态依赖扰动响应预测，并保留状态特异性。
papers.abstract_en: Predicting transcriptional responses to genetic perturbations is central to understanding gene function. Existing predictors primarily rely on transcriptomic measurements, although chromatin accessibility provides complementary information about the cellular context in which perturbations act. Using this information requires linking chromatin context to specific perturbations and accounting for baseline differences between independently sampled control and perturbed populations. We propose ChromaPert, a chromatin-informed framework for predicting state-dependent perturbation responses. ChromaPert combines molecular and DNA-informed locus priors with paired control RNA--ATAC features to jointly represent target identity and measured cellular context. Its Chromatin-Guided Response Router (CGRR) builds a source bank of control-derived expression offsets and retrieves relevant sources using perturbation/locus or control-ATAC similarity. These offsets account for baseline differences, while conditional transport flow learns the remaining response. Across three unseen-target and held-out-state settings on K562 CAT-ATAC and Perturb-Multiome, ChromaPert achieves the highest all-gene response correlation among evaluated methods. When transferring known perturbations to held-out states, it improves correlation by 23.2% across all genes and 46.2% for the twenty most responsive genes over the strongest respective baselines. Correct RNA--ATAC pairing improves recovery of chromatin-associated response slopes over shuffled pairing, while cross-state predictions retain state-specific responses to the same perturbation.
